item.title: Fiji Pearls edge Cook Islands 65-63 in Oceania qualifiers opener
item.description: The Crest Fiji Pearls have won their first game at the Oceania Netball World Cup qualifiers edging the Cook Islands 65-63. The lead went back and forth between the two sides with Cook Islands leading 36-32 at half time.
item.content:encoded:
The Crest Fiji Pearls have won their first game at the Oceania Netball World Cup qualifiers edging the Cook Islands 65-63.

The lead went back and forth between the two sides with Cook Islands leading 36-32 at half time.

The Fiji Pearls fought back in the final quarter to take the game.

They will now face Samoa at 3pm tomorrow.

The Fiji Pearls will then play hosts Tonga at 3pm Thursday, with their final game against Papua New Guinea at 3pm Friday.

Only the top two teams from the Qualifiers will make it through to the 2027 Netball World Cup in Sydney.

item.title: Ba FC President dedicates Ba’s historic treble to loyal supporters
item.description: Dayal’s Steel Ba FC President Praneel Dayal has dedicated the team’s historic 2026 treble to the people of Ba and its loyal supporters. Ba won the BiC Fiji FACT, Extra Premier League and Extra Battle of the Giants titles this season, while the team has also qualified for next year’s OFC Men’s Champions League after winning the league.
item.content:encoded:
Dayal’s Steel Ba FC President Praneel Dayal has dedicated the team’s historic 2026 treble to the people of Ba and its loyal supporters.

Ba won the BiC Fiji FACT, Extra Premier League and Extra Battle of the Giants titles this season, while the team has also qualified for next year’s OFC Men’s Champions League after winning the league.

Dayal says the success belongs to every Ba supporter who continued to believe in the team.

He says the achievement follows a promise he made to supporters after Ba lost to Rewa in last year’s Inter-District Championship final.

Dayal says seeing supporters leave the stadium heartbroken after the defeat strengthened his determination to restore Ba’s glory days.

He says the team remained firm through difficult decisions and challenges, supported by the prayers of thousands of supporters.

Dayal says the three trophies now sit proudly in Ba’s cabinet and the team will represent Ba and Fiji at the regional level next year.

He says the success belongs not only to the board, coaching staff and players, but also to the supporters who stood by the team throughout the season.

item.title: 15 Bulikula Rugby League World Cup players still fighting for finals glory
item.description: The Fiji National Rugby League confirmed this to fijivillage News, saying with the 2026 Rugby League World Cup now fast approaching, 15 members of the Bulikula squad remain in finals contention across the NRLW, Queensland’s BMD Premiership and the NSW Women’s Premiership. They say for Fiji, it is an encouraging sign of the depth and quality available to the national women’s programme.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji National Rugby League confirmed this to fijivillage News, saying with the 2026 Rugby League World Cup now fast approaching, 15 members of the Bulikula squad remain in finals contention across the NRLW, Queensland’s BMD Premiership and the NSW Women’s Premiership.

They say for Fiji, it is an encouraging sign of the depth and quality available to the national women’s programme.

The Bulikula will make history this year by appearing at their first Rugby League World Cup after qualifying through the 2025 World Series in Canada.

Fiji thrashed Nigeria 62–4 in the final to secure the final women’s World Cup berth.

FNRL says that as preparations for the World Cup intensify, a number of Fiji’s players are still chasing domestic titles with their respective clubs.

The Women's Rugby League World Cup starts on the 8th of October , and runs through November 24, 2026.

item.title: Buadromo named IOC Believe in Sport Ambassador for Dakar 2026
item.description: Fiji’s Olympic swimmer Matelita Buadromo has been named one of six IOC Believe in Sport Ambassadors for the Youth Olympic Games Dakar 2026 and is the only ambassador from Oceania. item.content:encoded:
Fiji’s Olympic swimmer Matelita Buadromo has been named one of six IOC Believe in Sport Ambassadors for the Youth Olympic Games Dakar 2026 and is the only ambassador from Oceania.

Believe in Sport is an International Olympic Committee campaign aimed at tackling competition manipulation, which can involve athletes deliberately underperforming or losing, or officials deliberately making incorrect calls.

Buadromo represented Fiji in swimming at the London 2012 and Rio 2016 Olympic Games.

She has been involved in efforts to tackle competition manipulation since 2022, and her ambassador role will continue through the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, Pacific Games Tahiti 2027 and LA28.

In Dakar, the ambassadors will meet with young athletes, coaches and families to discuss how athletes can be approached in relation to competition manipulation and where such approaches can be reported.

Around 2,700 young athletes will compete in Dakar from 31st October to 13th November, in what will be the first Olympic sports event held on African soil.

item.title: Crest Fiji Pearls in high spirits ahead of crucial Cook Islands clash today
item.description: Fiji Netball has confirmed that the Pearls enjoyed a positive final session, with the players showing plenty of energy and enthusiasm as they put the finishing touches to their preparations. They say the players are ready for a match that could set the tone for their campaign in Tonga.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Netball has confirmed that the Pearls enjoyed a positive final session, with the players showing plenty of energy and enthusiasm as they put the finishing touches to their preparations.

They say the players are ready for a match that could set the tone for their campaign in Tonga.

Fiji's preparations have been built around taking the tournament one match at a time, with head coach Michelle Parsons stressing the importance of treating every game like a final.

Parsons says the team knows there is little room for error in a five-day qualifying tournament featuring Fiji, the Cook Islands, Tonga, Samoa and Papua New Guinea.

The players' high spirits will be welcomed by the coaching staff, but the real test begins when the first whistle sounds.

The Fiji Pearls will face the Cook Islands today at 5pm.
